title: Google Search Design
description: Understand how Google designs its search infrastructure to process billions of queries daily through crawling, indexing, ranking, and distributed retrieval.

data.text: Google Search processes over 8.5 billion queries per day across trillions of web pages. Its infrastructure is a distributed systems landmark, combining web crawling, inverted indexing, MapReduce processing, and machine learning ranking into a system that returns results in under 200 milliseconds.

Every search query goes through four stages: receiving the query, parsing and expanding it, retrieving matching documents from the index, and ranking them by relevance. The first three stages must complete in under 100 milliseconds to meet latency targets.

    D --> E[Index Shard Router]

    E --> G[Shard 2]

    G --> I
    H --> I
    I --> J[Ranking - PageRank + ML]
    J --> K[Result Page]

data.text: Googlebot crawls the web continuously, fetching pages and following links. Fetched pages are parsed, stripped of HTML tags, and tokenized into words. The resulting tokens are stored in an inverted index: for each word, a list of documents containing it.

data.title: Inverted Index
data.text: An inverted index maps each word to the documents containing it. Without it, searching billions of documents would require scanning every document on every query. The inverted index reduces search to a simple lookup.

The inverted index is too large for a single machine. Google shards it by word prefix or document ID across thousands of machines. Each query is sent to all shards in parallel, and results are merged before ranking.

terms.definition: A data structure mapping words to the documents containing them; the foundation of search engines.
An automated system that discovers and fetches web pages for indexing.
A link-analysis algorithm that measures the importance of web pages based on inbound link quality.

data.title: Google Search Lessons
points: Inverted indexing makes text search feasible at web scale
Sharding enables parallel queries across thousands of machines
Ranking is a separate, ML-enhanced stage after retrieval
MapReduce powers batch indexing while serving uses custom clusters
Crawling, indexing, and serving are fully decoupled pipelines
data.takeaway: Google Search shows that breaking a complex problem into independent, parallelizable stages is the key to sub-second latency at web scale.

data.title: Build a Mini Search Engine
data.description: Build a search engine for 1 million documents. Design the inverted index structure, specify the sharding strategy, and estimate the query latency for a 3-word query across 10 shards.
data.expectedOutcome: Inverted index in Redis or Elasticsearch. Shard by document ID hash. 10 shards in parallel = ~20ms for top-10 results from each shard + 10ms merge.
